column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:parselang module + the core `parse` word
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# `parse <kind> <opts?> <source>` is the sibling of `mini`: it expands at the
# call site to the STANDARD parser call `ParseLang.parse_<kind> <source> <opts>
# end`. Unlike `mini`, the `source` is the REQUIRED LAST surface arg (a String
# or a {src:…} Source map) and `opts` is the optional MIDDLE one — disambiguated
# by arity. A parser returns Any (an AST, a transduction, …). `ParseLang.register`
# installs AQL fns as parsers; `ParseLang.kinds` lists them; `ParseLang.source`
# resolves a source value to its String. These rows register a small `calc`
# parser whose AST is the token list `[left op right]` (built by StringUtil.split
# on the resolved source). A {file:…} source is deferred in v1.
# §1  parse — an AQL-registered parser returning a tokenization
aql:parselang import end  "aql:string-util" import end  ParseLang.register calc (fn [[source:Any opts:Map] [List] [StringUtil.split ' ' (ParseLang.source source)]]) end  (parse calc 'x + y') get 1
column3: the parsed operator token

column1: aql:parselang import end  "aql:string-util" import end  ParseLang.register calc (fn [[source:Any opts:Map] [List] [StringUtil.split ' ' (ParseLang.source source)]]) end  (parse calc 'x + y') get 0
column3: the left operand token

column1: aql:parselang import end  "aql:string-util" import end  ParseLang.register calc (fn [[source:Any opts:Map] [List] [StringUtil.split ' ' (ParseLang.source source)]]) end  (parse calc '3 * 4') get 2
column3: operands are arbitrary tokens, not fixed identifiers

column1: # §5  ini — the built-in INI parser (github.com/tabnas/ini/go). No host
#     registration needed: importing the module is enough. Top-level
#     `key = value` lines become Map fields, `[section]` headers nest a Map,
#     and a recognised boolean decodes to a Boolean.
aql:parselang import end  (parse ini 'b = hello') get 'b'
column3: a top-level key/value decodes to a String field

column1: aql:parselang import end  (parse ini {src:'b = hello'}) get 'b'
column3: a {src:…} Source map resolves like every other parser

column1: aql:parselang import end  ((parse ini 'a = 1\n[sec]\nx = true') get 'sec') get 'x'
column3: a [section] header nests a Map; a recognised boolean decodes to a Boolean

column1: aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_ini 'b = hello' {} end) get 'b'
column3: parse is pure sugar — the desugared standard call is equivalent

column3: {file:…} source is deferred in v1, ini included

column1: # §6  the rest of the tabnas parser family (github.com/tabnas/*) — all built
#     in, all reached the same way. These pin the desugared standard call so
#     every parser export is covered; the JSON family + yaml/zon return the
#     decoded top level, csv/markdown a List of rows/blocks, toml/xml/feed a Map.
aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_json '{"a":1,"b":"hi"}' {} end) get 'b'
column3: JSON object → Map

column1: aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_jsonic '{a:1, b:"hi"}' {} end) get 'b'
column3: jsonic (relaxed JSON): unquoted keys

column1: aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_json5 '{a:1, b:0x10}' {} end) get 'b'
column3: JSON5: hex literal decodes to an Integer

column1: aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_jsonc '{"a":1, "b":2}' {} end) get 'b'
column3: JSONC (JSON with comments)

column1: aql:parselang import end  ((ParseLang.parse_csv 'a,b\n1,2' {} end) get 0) get 1
column3: CSV → List of rows; row 0 is the header

column1: aql:parselang import end  (ParseLang.parse_toml 'b = "hi"' {} end) get 'b'
column3: TOML table → Map

column3: YAML mapping → Map

column3: ZON (Zig object notation) → Map

column3: Markdown → List of blocks

column3: RSS/Atom feed → normalised atom-shaped Map
